messages:
nora: Hit a weird cursor-corruption issue in the sample paginator today. After a few retries we start getting duplicate pages + cursor jumps and the import shows gaps. Repro is deterministic for me.

devon: Yikes. Which SDK and sample?

nora: js-sdk@2.7, sampleapps/stream-import, concurrency=6, windowSize=192. The server occasionally returns 500 for transient blobs. When a page retry happens the paginator sometimes resumes from an earlier cursor value.

isa: Do you have logs or a minimal trace? This sounds like retry + cursor advancement race.

nora: Logs (trimmed):
```
2027-03-03T09:12:01.001Z DEBUG paginator: acquire-slot id=92 cursor="c_123"
2027-03-03T09:12:01.050Z DEBUG transport -> /v1/items id=92 resp=500
2027-03-03T09:12:01.051Z DEBUG retry: schedule id=92 backoff=120ms
2027-03-03T09:12:01.052Z DEBUG paginator: advance-cursor to "c_125" (optimistic)
2027-03-03T09:12:01.173Z DEBUG retry: retrying id=92 cursor="c_123"
2027-03-03T09:12:01.174Z DEBUG transport -> /v1/items id=92 resp=200 items=[...]
2027-03-03T09:12:01.175Z DEBUG paginator: accept-page id=92 cursor="c_123"
2027-03-03T09:12:01.176Z DEBUG paginator: current-cursor="c_123" (but we advanced to c_125 earlier)
```
The optimistic cursor advance is not reconciled with the actual accepted page cursor, so later pages are fetched from c_125 and we miss c_124 or process c_124 twice depending on timing.

ryan: That's a subtle one. Looks like the paginator optimistically advances the cursor when a request is dispatched to keep throughput high, but retries that succeed later bring back an older cursor and we never reconcile the interim advance. Leads to holes or duplicates.

devon: We only implemented optimistic cursor movement to allow continuous windowing without per-request blocking. But we never stored per-slot expected-cursor metadata to reconcile on success/failure.

isa: Two approaches: A) attach a per-request id + expected-cursor and only advance the global cursor when the lowest outstanding request is accepted (strict ordering), or B) make cursors immutable by attaching an idempotency token to each page and let the server dedupe older commits. Option A maintains client-side linearity but may reduce throughput; option B shifts complexity to server.

nora: I prefer A for now since we can't guarantee server-side dedupe for all customers. We can implement a lightweight per-slot checkpoint: each slot holds expected-cursor; global-cursor is the minimum of (accepted cursors + highest slot indices) so we never advance beyond any pending lower cursors.

devon: Also need to make retries idempotent: include page_id in the request body and ensure the SDK won't requeue the same page as a new page if the server responds slowly.

ryan: For parity: python/go SDKs currently do strict per-slot checkpointing (hence they didn't hit this), node implemented optimistic advance for throughput. We should align node to parity and add a config option optimisticCursor:true|false (default false).

isa: Add tests: unit test that simulates out-of-order retries causing cursor regression and asserts no holes; e2e that injects intermittent 500s and validates ordered processing of page IDs. Also add a chaos test that mixes retries + reconnects.

nora: I hacked a local fix: changed paginator to keep per-slot expectedCursor and only update globalCursor when the head slot reports accepted cursor >= globalCursorNext. With that the repro fails to reproduce. Perf impact minimal in my bench.

devon: Great — please open a sampleapps branch with repro and the fix, include unit+e2e tests. We'll also add an observability metric paginator.cursor_reconciliations and an alert when reconciliation_count > threshold.

ci-bot: CI started for branch nora/paginator-cursor-reconcile #3

ryan: For docs and DX: update the quickstart to mention cursor semantics and why optimistic behavior can be toggled. Add a short note in the SDK changelog about this regression and recommended upgrade path.

isa: Follow-up: consider offering an advanced "server-ack" mode where the server explicitly acknowledges cursor commits; that'd let us safely optimistically advance in the future. But let's do the parity fix first.

nora: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/sampleapps/pull/789 — includes per-slot expectedCursor, page_id injection, tests, and a feature flag optimisticCursor (off by default). Tagging @devon @isa for review.

ci-bot: CI passed for PR nora/paginator-cursor-reconcile #789 (unit: 16/16, e2e: 1/1) :white_check_mark:

ryan: Excellent. After merge let's backport to the 2.x branch and add a KB about "missing pages / duplicates during retries" for customers.

nora: Thanks team. This was a nasty one to catch in the wild.
